findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "trouver_expert" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Call this when the user needs a trustworthy real-estate professional in a Canadian city or neighbourhood: real-estate broker, mortgage broker, home inspector, n…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "contacter_expert" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call this ONLY when the user explicitly asks to contact, reach out to, or request a quote/appointment from a Payotte-listed professional. DOUBLE OPT-IN: this to…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contacter_expert · Private data: trouver_expert, verifier_titre, taux_courants, contacter_expert · Public sink: contacter_expert.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contacter_expert · Private data: trouver_expert, verifier_titre, taux_courants, contacter_expert · Public sink: contacter_expert

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "trouver_expert" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
